Today, I had the pleasure of engaging with United Nations colleagues working across jobs, health, gender, and sustainable development in Bosnia and Herzegovina—areas all connected by one common thread: a just energy transition.

In today’s geopolitical context—marked by price volatility, supply risks, and shifting energy alliances—this transition becomes a clear opportunity for BiH:
•	From coal dependence to economic diversification – coal still accounts for 47% of energy supply and over $400 million in exports, but transitioning can unlock new industries and reduce exposure to external shocks 
•	From energy vulnerability to security and growth – with a target of 43.6% renewables by 2030, BiH can strengthen energy independence while creating new economic opportunities.

The transition is about transforming an existing energy system into a more competitive, resilient, and future-ready economy. How do we accelerate and align this shift?

1.	Strengthen the grid to drive growth: With over $6 billion needed and renewables rising, the priority is integration. A stronger, digital grid unlocks capacity, reliability, and competitiveness.

2.	Turn coal into a just transition pathway: Coal supports jobs and exports but also creates an entry point for reskilling and new industries. This is strategic to shift from job loss and brain drain to creating jobs and retaining talent.

3.	Make efficiency an economic strategy: With buildings using over 50% of energy, efficiency is the fastest way to cut costs, improve air quality, and strengthen resilience, especially when scaled through data and digital tools.

4.	Unlocking private investment to scale bankable energy pipelines – with over $405 million in electricity exports, BiH has a strong foundation to attract investment and position itself as a competitive clean energy supplier

UNDP, together with the wider UN system, stands ready to support Bosnia and Herzegovina in shaping and delivering this just energy transition pathway.
